name: Thinking Philosophically About Science
description: Science is humanity's most systematic and powerful method for understanding the world. But what kind of knowledge does science produce, and what assumptions about the world does it bring with it? This course offers an accessible philosophical introduction to the foundations and methods of scientific inquiry. Students examine how theories relate to evidence, how experiments and models function, and what reasoning strategies underlie scientific knowledge. They also ask what distinguishes science from non-science, whether theories reveal the truth about the world, and how values and objectivity shape scientific practice. The goal is to help students become not merely practitioners of science but thoughtful and reflective thinkers about it.
